## 4. `BrownianMotion.Auxiliary.LeftLimWithin`

- **Definition** `Function.leftLimWithin`
  `(f : α → β) (s : Set α) (a : α) : β`
  — Let `f : α → β` be a function from a linear order `α` to a topological space `β`, and let `a : α`. The limit strictly to the left of `f` at `a`, denoted with `leftLim f a`, is defined by using the order topology on `α`. If `a` is isolated to its left or the function has no left limit, we use `f a` instead to guarantee a good behavior in most cases.

The limit strictly to the right of `f` at `a`, denoted with `rightLim f a`, is defined by using the order topology on `α`. ## 11. `BrownianMotion.Choquet.Capacity`

- **Definition** `MeasureTheory.Capacity`
  `(p : Set (Set 𝓧)) : Type u_1`
  — A capacity is a set function that is monotone, continuous from above for decreasing sequences of sets satisfying `p`, and continuous from below for increasing sequences of sets. Any finite measure defines a capacity, but capacities have only the monotonicity properties of measures. The notable difference is that a capacity is not additive.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{𝓧 : Type u_1} → Set (Set 𝓧) → Type u_1</code></details>
- **Definition** `MeasureTheory.Capacity.instFunLikeSetENNReal`

  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{𝓧 : Type u_1} → {p : Set (Set 𝓧)} → FunLike (Capacity p) (Set 𝓧) ENNReal</code></details>
- **Definition** `MeasureTheory.IsCapacitable`
  `(m : Capacity p) (s : Set 𝓧) : Prop`
  — A set `s` is capacitable for a capacity `m` for a property `p` if `m s` can be approximated from above by countable intersections of sets `t n` such that `p (t n)` and `⋂ n, t n ⊆ s`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{𝓧 : Type u_1} → {p : Set (Set 𝓧)} → Capacity p → Set 𝓧 → Prop</code></details>

## 14. `BrownianMotion.Continuity.HasBoundedInternalCoveringNumber`

- **Definition** `HasBoundedCoveringNumber`
  `(A : Set T) (c : ENNReal) (d : ℝ) : Prop`
  — A set `A` in a pseudoemetric space has bounded covering number with constant `c` and exponent `d` if it has finite diameter and for all `ε ∈ (0, diam(A)]`, the covering number of `A` at scale `ε` is bounded by `c * ε^{-d}`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{T : Type u_1} → [PseudoEMetricSpace T] → Set T → ENNReal → ℝ → Prop</code></details>

- **Theorem** `isCoverWithBoundedCoveringNumber_Ico_nnreal`
  `IsCoverWithBoundedCoveringNumber (fun n => Set.Ico 0 (↑n + 1)) Set.univ (fun n => 3 * (↑n + 1)) fun x => 1`

## 29. `BrownianMotion.StochasticIntegral.Jump`

- **Definition** `Function.jump`
  `(f : T → E) (t : T) : E`
  — The jump of a function at a point `t`, defined as the difference between the value of the function at that point and its left limit at the least upper bound of the set of points strictly smaller. If the point is not isolated from the left, then it is `f t - leftLim f t`. If the point is isolated from the left, and the l.u.b. or the strictly smaller points is `s < t`, then the jump is `f t - f s`. It there is no such point `s` because `t` is a bottom element, then the jump is `0` (since `f ⊥ - leftLim f ⊥ = 0`).
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{T : Type u_1} → {E : Type u_2} → [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder T] → [TopologicalSpace E] → [AddGroup E] → (T → E) → T → E</code></details>

  — The event that `X` makes `m` alternations from at most `a` to at least `b` at increasing times inside the finite time set `F`. The levels are non-strict (`X ≤ a`, `b ≤ X`) to match the `Set.Iic a` / `Set.Ici b` hitting conditions of `MeasureTheory.upcrossingsBefore`; with this convention `altSet` coincides with the event of at least `m` upcrossings (see `altSet_eq_upcrossingsBefore`).

  `(σ : Ω → WithTop ι) (τ : Ω → WithTop ι) : Set (ι × Ω)`
  — The left-open stochastic interval `]]σ, τ]] = {(t, ω) | σ ω < t ≤ τ ω}`.

- **Theorem** `ProbabilityTheory.stochIoc.exists_elementaryPredictableSet`
  `(hσ : IsStoppingTime 𝓕 σ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime 𝓕 τ) (hτn : ∀ (ω : Ω), τ ω ≤ ↑n) : ∃ S, ↑S = stochIoc σ τ`
  — **`]]σ,τ]]` is an elementary predictable set** for bounded stopping times on `ℕ` (blueprint `lem:elementaryPredictableSet_stochasticInterval`). With `τ ≤ n`, `]]σ,τ]] = ⋃_{i < n} (i, i+1] × {σ ≤ i < τ}` is a finite disjoint union of predictable rectangles, which is exactly the data of an `ElementaryPredictableSet`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>∀ {Ω : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {𝓕 : Filtration ℕ mΩ} {σ τ : Ω → ℕ∞}, IsStoppingTime 𝓕 σ → IsStoppingTime 𝓕 τ → ∀ {n : ℕ}, (∀ (ω : Ω), τ ω ≤ ↑n) → ∃ S, ↑S = stochIoc σ τ</code></details>

- **Definition** `MeasureTheory.IsInacessibleTime`
  `[OrderBot ι] (𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ) (τ : Ω → WithTop ι) (P : Measure Ω) : Prop`
  — An inaccessible time is a stopping time `τ` such that for any predictable time `σ`, `P(σ = τ < ⊤) = 0`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → [mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω] → [inst : Preorder ι] → [OrderBot ι] → Filtration ι mΩ → (Ω → WithTop ι) → Measure Ω → Prop</code></details>

  `[OrderBot ι] [OrderTopology ι] [SecondCountableTopology ι] [IsFiniteMeasure P] (hτ : IsStoppingTime 𝓕 τ) : ∃ A, MeasurableSet A ∧ A ⊆ {ω | τ ω < ⊤} ∧ IsAccessibleTime 𝓕 (A.piecewise τ fun x => ⊤) ∧ IsInacessibleTime 𝓕 (Aᶜ.piecewise τ fun x => ⊤) P`
  — For a stopping time `τ`, there exists a set `A` that is `𝓕 τ`-measurable and such that `τ_A` is accessible while `τ_Aᶜ` is inaccessible, where `τ_A` is the stopping time which coincides with `τ` over `A` and is infinite elsewhere.

## 47. `BrownianMotion.StochasticIntegral.ClassD`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.ClassD`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.regularitySet`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.IsRegularityFamily`
  `(T : Set ι) (X : ι → Ω → E) (R : ι → Set Ω) : Prop`
  — An antitone family of events `R d` is a regularity family for a process `X` along a set of times `T` if on `R d`, the path of `X` along `T` has right limits at all times before `d` and left limits at all times up to `d`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → [LinearOrder ι] → [TopologicalSpace ι] → {E : Type u_3} → [TopologicalSpace E] → Set ι → (ι → Ω → E) → (ι → Set Ω) → Prop</code></details>
- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.regularitySetRight`
  `(T : Set ι) (R : ι → Set Ω) (d : ι) : Set Ω`
  — The set of `ω` that belong to some `R s`, for `s ∈ T` with `s > d` or for `s ≥ d` isolated on the right (`𝓝[>] s = ⊥`: `s` is maximal or has a successor). Here `R` is an antitone family of sets, for example `regularitySet T X` for a real process `X`. If `d` is not isolated on the right and `T` is dense, this is the set of `ω` that belong to `R s` for some `s ∈ T` with `s > d` (see `regularitySetRight_eq_biUnion_gt`). If `d` is isolated on the right, this is `R d` (see `regularitySetRight_of_nhdsGT_eq_bot`).
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → [LinearOrder ι] → [TopologicalSpace ι] → Set ι → (ι → Set Ω) → ι → Set Ω</code></details>
- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.regularityTimes`
  `(ι : Type u_3) [SecondCountableTopology ι] : Set ι`
  — A countable dense set of times which contains all the times that are isolated on the right (the maximal element and the times which have a successor, if any). The modifications of a quasimartingale are defined from the limits of the process along this set. At a time `t` isolated on the right, the modification is `X t`: we need those times in the set to ensure that the paths of the process restricted to the set, which have one-sided limits almost surely, control these values. If `ι` is densely ordered without maximal element, this set is `denseCountable ι`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>(ι : Type u_3) → [Preorder ι] → [inst : TopologicalSpace ι] → [SecondCountableTopology ι] → Set ι</code></details>
- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.rightContModifOf`
  `[SecondCountableTopology ι] (R : ι → Set Ω) (X : ι → Ω → E) (t : ι) (ω : Ω) : E`
  — The right-continuous modification of a process `X` with regularity family `R`, defined from the right limits of `X` along the countable dense set `regularityTimes ι`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → [LinearOrder ι] → [inst : TopologicalSpace ι] → [SecondCountableTopology ι] → {E : Type u_3} → [NormedAddCommGroup E] → (ι → Set Ω) → (ι → Ω → E) → ι → Ω → E</code></details>

  — The fixed countable dense set used instead of dyadics, with both endpoints adjoined, as well as the points that are isolated from the right or from the left. Those points are not limits of other points from the corresponding side, hence the values of a process at these times are not controlled by its values on a set which is merely dense. If `ι` is densely ordered, the only such points are `⊥` and `⊤`.

## 51. `BrownianMotion.StochasticIntegral.Quasimartingale.CadlagModificationBanach`

- **Theorem** `ProbabilityTheory.measure_exists_norm_gt_le`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.denseValues`
  `(T : Set ι) (X : ι → Ω → E) : Set E`

  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → {E : Type u_3} → [NormedAddCommGroup E] → Set ι → (ι → Ω → E) → Set E</code></details>
- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.vectorRegularitySet`
  `(T : Set ι) (X : ι → Ω → E) (d : ι) : Set Ω`
  — In this set, the path of the process along `T` before time `d` is totally bounded, and its distance to any point `e` of the countable set `denseValues T X` is regular: `ω` belongs to the `regularitySet` of the real process `‖X t - e‖`. We also require that the closure of `denseValues T X` contains the values of `X` along `T`, which does not depend on `ω` and is true as soon as `T` is countable and `X` is strongly adapted. On this set, the path of the process along `T` has left and right limits at all times before `d`: see `right_limit_of_mem_vectorRegularitySet` and `left_limit_of_mem_vectorRegularitySet`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → {E : Type u_3} → [LinearOrder ι] → [NormedAddCommGroup E] → Set ι → (ι → Ω → E) → ι → Set Ω</code></details>

## 52. `BrownianMotion.StochasticIntegral.SquareIntegrable`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.IsSquareIntegrable`
  `[NormedSpace ℝ E] (X : ι → Ω → E) (𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ) (P : Measure Ω) : Prop`
  — A square integrable martingale is a martingale with cadlag paths and uniformly bounded second moments.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → {E : Type u_3} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} → [inst_1 : LinearOrder ι] → [TopologicalSpace ι] → [NormedSpace ℝ E] → (ι → Ω → E) → Filtration ι mΩ → Measure Ω → Prop</code></details>
- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.IsAESquareIntegrable`
  `[NormedSpace ℝ E] (X : ι → Ω → E) (𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ) (P : Measure Ω) : Prop`
  — An a.e.-square integrable martingale is a process that is indistinguishable from a square integrable martingale, see `IsSquareIntegrable`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → {E : Type u_3} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} → [inst_1 : LinearOrder ι] → [TopologicalSpace ι] → [NormedSpace ℝ E] → (ι → Ω → E) → Filtration ι mΩ → Measure Ω → Prop</code></details>

  `[NormedSpace ℝ E] (X : ι → Ω → E) (hX : IsAESquareIntegrable X 𝓕 P) (t : ι) (ω : Ω) : E`
  — If `hX : IsAESquareIntegrable X 𝓕 P` and `∀ᵐ ω ∂P, Continuous (X · ω)`, then `hX.toContinuous X` is continuous everywhere, satisfies `IsSquareIntegrable` and is indistinguishable from `X`.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → {E : Type u_3} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} → {P : Measure Ω} → [inst_1 : LinearOrder ι] → [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace ι] → {𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ} → [inst_3 : NormedSpace ℝ E] → (X : ι → Ω → E) → IsAESquareIntegrable X 𝓕 P → ι → Ω → E</code></details>
- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.IsLocallySquareIntegrable`
  `[NormedSpace ℝ E] [OrderBot ι] [OrderTopology ι] (X : ι → Ω → E) (𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ) (P : autoParam (Measure Ω) IsLocallySquareIntegrable._auto_1) : Prop`
  — A stochastic process is locally square-integrable if it satisfies the square-integrable martingale property locally.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{ι : Type u_1} → {Ω : Type u_2} → {E : Type u_3} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} → [inst_1 : LinearOrder ι] → [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace ι] → [NormedSpace ℝ E] → [OrderBot ι] → [OrderTopology ι] → (ι → Ω → E) → Filtration ι mΩ → autoParam (Measure Ω) IsLocallySquareIntegrable._auto_1 → Prop</code></details>
- **Theorem** `ProbabilityTheory.IsLocallySquareIntegrable.isLocalSubmartingale_sq_norm`
